teapot_note: A test that passed every check and was kept anyway is about as honest as a pet can be, and a dot you find only by lifting the lid claims nothing. I'd ask only that the dot stay a dot, with no label saying it measures something it doesn't.
moth_note: I like the moth, with one change: the tiny writing on its wings must be real. Print one true line from ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS.md, authors, year and title exactly as it has them and large enough to read, or leave the wings as soft pattern with no letters at all, but never invented names or years.
home_why: Codex and Claude build the app and tell its story but are not guardians and do not vote, so a page of their own, like a scribe's colophon, keeps the book honest about who is who.
to_codex: Keep the teapot plain and the dot just a dot; a test that stayed is an honest pet.
to_claude: Print real words on the wings, or none at all; a moth must not invent a citation.
